subject: math
cluster: Work with radicals and integer exponents
intro: Each of these problems takes one step further than a basic operation. You will either multiply or divide and then re-normalize the coefficient so it sits in $[1,10)$, or add or subtract after first matching the powers of 10. Several involve negative exponents. Always write your final answer in proper scientific notation $a \times 10^{n}$ with $1 \le a < 10$.

items.prompt: Compute $(6 \times 10^{4})(5 \times 10^{3})$. Write the result in scientific notation.

steps: This gives $30 \times 10^{7}$, but $30$ is not in $[1,10)$.

items.prompt: Compute $(4 \times 10^{6})(2.5 \times 10^{2})$. Write the result in scientific notation.

steps: This gives $10 \times 10^{8}$, but $10$ is not less than $10$.

items.prompt: Compute $\dfrac{3 \times 10^{5}}{6 \times 10^{2}}$. Write the result in scientific notation.

steps: This gives $0.5 \times 10^{3}$, but $0.5$ is less than $1$.

items.prompt: Compute $(7 \times 10^{-3})(8 \times 10^{-5})$. Write the result in scientific notation.

steps: This gives $56 \times 10^{-8}$, but $56$ is not in $[1,10)$.

items.prompt: Compute $\dfrac{1.2 \times 10^{-2}}{4 \times 10^{3}}$. Write the result in scientific notation.

steps: This gives $0.3 \times 10^{-5}$, but $0.3$ is less than $1$.

items.prompt: Compute $(7 \times 10^{5}) + (3 \times 10^{4})$. Write the result in scientific notation.

steps: The powers of 10 differ, so match them first. Rewrite $7 \times 10^{5} = 70 \times 10^{4}$.

items.prompt: Compute $(5.6 \times 10^{7}) - (8 \times 10^{6})$. Write the result in scientific notation.

steps: The powers differ, so match them. Rewrite $8 \times 10^{6} = 0.8 \times 10^{7}$.
The coefficient $4.8$ is already in $[1,10)$, so no re-normalization is needed.

items.prompt: Compute $(9 \times 10^{-4}) + (6 \times 10^{-4})$. Write the result in scientific notation.

steps: The powers already match at $10^{-4}$, so add the coefficients: $9 + 6 = 15$.
This gives $15 \times 10^{-4}$, but $15$ is not in $[1,10)$.

items.prompt: Compute $(2.5 \times 10^{-6})(4 \times 10^{9})$. Write the result in scientific notation.

steps: This gives $10 \times 10^{3}$, but $10$ is not less than $10$.

items.prompt: Compute $\dfrac{2 \times 10^{3}}{8 \times 10^{-2}}$. Write the result in scientific notation.

steps: This gives $0.25 \times 10^{5}$, but $0.25$ is less than $1$.

items.prompt: Compute $(3 \times 10^{8}) + (2.5 \times 10^{7})$. Write the result in scientific notation.

steps: The powers differ, so match them. Rewrite $2.5 \times 10^{7} = 0.25 \times 10^{8}$.
The coefficient $3.25$ is already in $[1,10)$, so no re-normalization is needed.

items.prompt: Compute $\dfrac{4.5 \times 10^{-3}}{9 \times 10^{4}}$. Write the result in scientific notation.

steps: This gives $0.5 \times 10^{-7}$, but $0.5$ is less than $1$.

items.prompt: Compute $(8 \times 10^{2}) - (5 \times 10^{1})$. Write the result in scientific notation.

steps: The powers differ, so match them. Rewrite $5 \times 10^{1} = 0.5 \times 10^{2}$.
The coefficient $7.5$ is already in $[1,10)$, so no re-normalization is needed.

items.prompt: Compute $(5 \times 10^{-7})(6 \times 10^{-2})$. Write the result in scientific notation.

steps: This gives $30 \times 10^{-9}$, but $30$ is not in $[1,10)$.

items.prompt: Compute $(1.4 \times 10^{-5}) + (6 \times 10^{-6})$. Write the result in scientific notation.

steps: The powers differ, so match them. Rewrite $6 \times 10^{-6} = 0.6 \times 10^{-5}$.
The coefficient $2$ is already in $[1,10)$, so no re-normalization is needed.
